_comment._span_caveat: THE STEP IS BELOW THE PER-SAMPLE CENTROID NOISE, AND THAT IS FINE, BUT KNOW IT: 0.219 px per step against fit_com's ~0.271 px frame-to-frame noise. What resolves it is averaging -- ~1150 settled samples per level puts the SEM at ~0.008 px, i.e. 4% of a step -- so a level's error bar is small but the RUN IS NOISE-LIMITED IN A WAY THE JULY ONE WAS NOT. Read the reported per-level SEM before trusting the slope. Sizing history, because the old caveat here got it wrong: this file was sized from Kx 4.05 at 32x32, and the correction is NOT just the (dim-1)/2 normalization -- 0.579 units/V at 64x64 is 18.2 px/V against 62.8 px/V in July, so the plant is ~3.4x weaker in px/V as well (conf_bode_par_x.json, _amplitude_2026_08_07). Travel is +-2.19 px, not the +-15 px the header used to claim nor the +-7 px the first correction guessed. NOTE ALSO THAT resp_max 0.9 CANNOT GUARD THIS: 0.9 units is 28 px, while the beam's tails start leaving the frame at ~3.5 px, so the guard never fires before truncation does. Check the px travel printed in the report, not resp_max.

params._roi_note: ROI, exposure AND gain copied from steering_par_fsp.json as of 2026-08-07 19:42, so this measures the plant the loop actually runs against. start 1076/404 lands the beam at in-frame (32.2, 31.3) against the 31.5 centre, re-probed from a capture AT THE OPERATING ROI. THE 1084/418 THIS FILE CARRIED WAS NEVER A TREE VALUE -- it took x from the bode configs (1084/414) and y from com_survey (1073/418), and both predate the 08-07 refocus. gain stays 0 because at the current source brightness every higher setting saturates the core (measured amp p50/saturation: gain 0 -> 137/1.66%, gain 50 -> 254/3.61%, saturated in over half of all frames). The beam walks several px per hour AND the park offset eats the same margin as the staircase: re-probe with contrib/calibration-scripts/configurations/probe_frame.json AND confirm against a capture at the operating ROI once |park| exceeds ~2 px. On 2026-08-07 a full-sensor probe and a cropped capture disagreed by 10 px in BOTH axes, so never re-derive from find_roi.py alone.

pipeline._comment: frame -> UDP viewer, so the beam can be watched walking the staircase

pipeline._note: fit_com, COPIED VERBATIM from steering_par_fsp.json as of 2026-08-07 19:42, so the gain is measured through the same sensor the loop uses -- steering moved from center_of_mass to fit_com on 2026-08-06 and a K measured through the old estimator is a K for a loop that no longer exists. Whole-frame window, so the +-2.19 px staircase never makes the window walk.
pipeline._gates: sigma_init 9.33 / sigma_min 2.8 / sigma_max 37.3 / min_amplitude 10 / window 0, re-derived 2026-08-07 19:42 after the beam was refocused twice during that session (sigma 6.55 -> 8.2 -> 5.21 -> 9.33 px). THE 08-06 SET THIS FILE USED TO CARRY (sigma_init 6.55, window 55, min_amplitude 21.39) IS RETIRED: 21.39 is 0.1x a 213.9 amplitude the beam has not reached since, and together with camera gain 0 it is exactly the combination that made the tracker reject 300 frames in a row and re-acquire several times a second WITH THE MIRROR PARKED on 2026-08-07 18:03 -- which in a staircase would have frozen whole levels. window 0 = whole frame because at sigma 9.33 a +/-4 sigma window is 75 px, larger than the 64 px frame: a 55 px window clips the beam's own tails, and a clipped tail biases the centroid inward, i.e. straight into the slope. RE-DERIVE with contrib/calibration-scripts/tools/com_survey_run.sh after any refocus or source change, and take the values from steering, not from here.
pipeline._holds: WHAT THE FROZEN-LEVEL GUARD DOES AND DOES NOT CATCH. gain_test excludes a level whose settled samples are ALL bit-identical, which is what fit_com publishes when every fit in the window fails -- so a fully lost level is still caught, exactly as with center_of_mass. IT DOES NOT CATCH A PARTIALLY HELD LEVEL: the test is `!wmoved`, so one differing sample clears it. With the 2026-08-07 chop (~46 Hz, 24.8% of frames dark, streaks exactly 13 frames) roughly a quarter of each level's ~1150 settled samples are held values. At DC that is nearly harmless -- a 13-frame hold is 6 ms inside a 500 ms settled window, so the held value comes from the SAME level and the mean is unbiased -- but it stops being harmless if the chop lengthens: the 08-06 source had stretches to 201 frames, long enough to carry the previous level's value across a step and pull the mean toward it, flattening K. Check the fit_com rejection rate and the dark-stretch length before trusting a slope. reacquire_after is 300 rather than the old 10 for the same reason as everywhere else in the tree: at 10 those stretches drop acquisition and re-search the window mid-staircase.

pipeline._comment: CoM -> UDP viewer so the tracked centroid can be overlaid

pipeline._note1: THE TEST. Drives element 1 (x) and watches element 1 of the CoM ([y, x]); y stays at 0 command, i.e. parked at 0 V.
pipeline._note2: 21 levels at 2 s each, traversed up and back down, give 84 s of staircase plus 10 s warmup and 2 s of ramp at each end. settle_frac 0.65 discards the first 35% and scores the final 1.3 s: about 3000 samples per visit at 2310 Hz, with extra time for optical or mechanical settling.
pipeline._updown: ON: the return staircase measures hysteresis and makes gain separable from linear beam drift. In a one-way rising staircase command and time are collinear, so the device cannot distinguish them. This matters on a rig whose K was measured drifting -39% per hour and whose beam walks several px per hour. Use the reported small-signal slope for fsp.K and check that the separate drift-aware full-range slope agrees; a material disagreement means the bench moved during the run.
pipeline._pixel_scale: MUST TRACK THE ROI: (dim-1)/2 = 31.5 px per unit at 64x64 (79.5 at the 160x160 on the ASI662MM, 15.5 at the old 32x32). Only affects the px figures in the report, never the slope.
pipeline._volts_per_unit: the DAC scale of the driven channel, +1.0 for x below (ch1 in the [-1, 1] scale array). Reporting only -- it converts the slope into px/V and mV/px and carries the optical sign.
pipeline._resp_max: 0.9 is left at the device default, but it is NOT the guard that matters here -- 0.9 units is 28 px, while the beam's tails start leaving the frame at ~3.5 px. It only catches a gross runaway. The real check is the px travel printed in the report against the 3.5 px ceiling in the header.

params.config: x/tilt DC gain through the PARPORT DAC (DAC81404, spi link, mmio, +-5 V range, mirror parked at 0 V), no coarse stage, ch0=y parked / ch1=x driven at scale +1.0 V/unit. ASI290MM 64x64 ROI 1076/404, exp 400, gain 0, fs ~2310 Hz, fit_com whole-frame sigma_init 9.33 max_iter 12. Compare the slope against the 2026-08-07 bode refit of fsm_bodex_par5/par6.dat: Kx 0.4054 +/- 0.0055 at 18:54, 0.579 at 18:10, drifting -39%/hour while the bench was being worked on. Do NOT compare against fsm_bodex_par2.dat's 4.05: that was 32x32 on the pre-swap camera, and the gap is not only the (dim-1)/2 normalization -- in px/V the plant is ~3.4x weaker as well. This slope, not par2, is what goes into steering_par_fsp.json's x.K.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC, wired exactly as steering_par_fsp.json: ch0 = y/tip at scale -1.0, ch1 = x/tilt at scale +1.0, offset 0. THE SIGNS WERE FLIPPED TO [-1, 1] ON 2026-08-07 AND CONFIRMED ON THE BENCH; the [1, -1] this file carried is the pre-flip convention, which is positive feedback on both axes. The scale signs MUST match the steering config -- the whole point of this run is to produce a K for that file, and a different sign convention here produces a K with the wrong sign for it.
pipeline._range: +-5 fixed. Auto-ranging is deliberately NOT enabled: a mid-sweep range change glitches the output for a frame and steps the quantization. The sweep stays within +-0.20 V. At 153 uV/LSB and 18.2 px/V, quantization is ~130x below the 0.364 px step.
pipeline._avss_note: AVSS must be -12 V on this rig for the bipolar range, as in every other parport_dac config here.
